//: The body in the cold and the heat (game src/game/survival/Warmth.js). Prologue design values, not CDDA's. Each of the six tracked parts carries a comfort number 0..100 (50 = neutral) that moves every minute toward an equilibrium: 50 + degreeWeight[part] x (feelsC + clothingC - comfortC[part]) + activity + hearth, less what wet cloth loses. clothingC = sum of garment warmth x effective coverage x warmthC, hands and feet folded into the arms and legs at foldShare. Calibrated on the whitelisted garments' warmth: a t-shirt and jeans is comfortable near 20 C, chilly at 12, cold at 5 and freezing under -5 within the hour; sweater, flannel jacket, knit hat, gloves and boots keep the core comfortable to about -5 in still air and chilly at -10; the best winter set holds -20.
//comfortC: The felt air, clothes included, at which a part sits at 50. The core wants the most; legs work and tolerate cold best.
//degreeWeight: Comfort points per degree away from comfortC.
//warmthC: Degrees one point of garment warmth is worth at full coverage.
//foldShare: Hands and feet lose heat far out of proportion to their size, so for warmth a glove or boot counts for this share of the limb (armour uses rules.combat.protection.foldShare instead).
//rate: Share of the gap to the equilibrium closed each minute. The core holds its heat longer than a limb.
//activity: Comfort points the body makes by activity level (sustenance.json actionActivities).
//exertion: Hard work heats the body (Warmth.activityName, for warmth only: what work burns in food stays sustenance.json's). practiceSkills: a practice recipe of these skills counts at this level whatever the recipe says; interactModes: breaking a fixture up; actions: action types, ahead of sustenance.json actionActivities. Calibrated so an hour of melee practice in a t-shirt, jeans and a sweater takes a rested body from comfortable to warm at 15 C and to hot or worse at 25 C; reading and bench work stay where they were.
//starved: A body past this starvation stage, or exhausted, cannot heat itself: comfort points lost on every part.
//sleepWake: 27.09.2026: a sleeper wakes when the core gets to `cold` or colder, or the torso to `hot` or hotter, but only on getting worse than it was since lying down, so a chilly bed can still be slept in. Freezing always wakes.
//bands: Lowest first: [below, id, label]. A part at or above the last `below` is burning.
//heat: The hot side. Above kneeAt a body sheds heat by sweating: only sweatShare of every comfort point past it counts, so layers matter less the hotter it gets and a shirt on a normal summer day stays at hot; very hot takes a warm spell on the road or heavy clothes in summer heat, burning heavy clothes and work in the heat. Shade and water cool hot air: above coolFromC the felt air takes terrainC, never below coolFromC. exhaustion: a burning torso loses hpPerHour and gains painPerHour of pain (not past painCap) while it lasts; at nothing it is heatstroke.
//hearth: A burning hearth on the hex. fireC is its radiant heat felt near it in the open; roomC is the air it can hold an enclosed room at, reached in proportion to the shelter's insulation. Rain or snow in the open halves the radiant part.
//shelter: Without a fire a shelter still pulls the felt air toward neutralC by insulation x stillPull (body heat trapped, shade in summer). Terrain gives shelter of its own: standing walls of a site, the trunks of a wood.

shelter.//carried: A tent or tarp in the pack or on the ground is pitched for the night: shelter while asleep only.

//bedding: Extra garment warmth on torso, arms and legs while asleep with this within reach (pack or ground). The best one counts, not the sum; a worn blanket already counts as clothing.
//wet: One number for the worn cloth, 0..1 (run.player.wet). Rain wets it at weather.json wetPerHour, less under a hood or rainproof outer layer and not at all under a roof; it dries in the open, fast by a fire, hardly at all below freezing. Wet cloth keeps only (1 - wet x clothingLoss) of its warmth.
//effects: What a band costs. The worst part names the survivor's state; `hands` reads the worse arm, `core` the worse of torso and head, the hot bands read the torso. moraleFloor: a standing mood entry that sinks to the floor and stays while the band holds (Morale.wear). metabolism multiplies the energy burned (cold eats the stockpile). workSpeed multiplies crafting, searching and gathering when the hands are this cold or the torso this hot. swingPercent / toHit add to the wound penalties the fight reads. thirst multiplies thirst and staminaRegen the stamina recovery while the torso is this hot.
//frostbite: Every full hour a limb or the head is freezing, chancePerHour (doubled when wet above wetAt) opens frostbite on it: body[part].frostbite. It costs like a gash (no infection race) and heals only while the part is at least `healAbove`, over healDays of such time.
//hypothermia: A freezing torso or head loses hpPerHour from that part; at nothing the survivor dies of the cold.
//sleep: Sleep is refused (too_cold) when the survivor is already very cold and the night by what is here would keep the core at `refuseAt` or worse.
//warmUp: The warm_up action: minutes offered, by a burning hearth on the hex. It is sitting close to the fire: activity counts as light work and the radiant heat doubles.
//heating: Automatic heat and cooling at the camp (electricity/Heating.js). A hearth, a brazier set down on the hex or an electric heater in AUTO comes on when the body is on.work or colder, in AUTO STRICT at on.craft or colder; it goes out again once every part is at offAt or warmer (a little inside comfortable, so it does not flicker on the edge). A fan or air conditioner comes on at coolOn.work / coolOn.craft or hotter and goes off when the torso is under coolOffBelow.
//keepFire: Sleeping with 'keep the fire burning': the fuel within reach must cover planHours of burning or the sleep dialog refuses and names the shortfall; through the night the hearth is topped up to topUpToMinutes whenever it falls under topUpBelowMinutes.
//wood: The stockpile arithmetic the explainer shows (computed from the fuel's burn time and weight, fuelItem burning nightHours): the design targets are a long winter night by a fire ring in the open for about 20 kg of wood and a stone fireplace heating a hut for about 8 kg; a day gathering fallen wood in a forest brings about forestDayKg, mostly sticks that flare and are gone.
//calibration: Rows the tests hold the model to: an outfit (worn ids), the still air, the activity and the band each named part must be (at the equilibrium).
